tasks.title: BUG: marking invoices paid manually broken
tasks.notes: When client pays outside QB and QB can't detect it, manually marking as paid navigates to the project but the invoice status doesn't update correctly.

prep.what: Fix the manual invoice mark-as-paid flow so that when a client pays outside QuickBooks and you confirm it manually, the invoice status correctly transitions to paid.
prep.understand: The difference between QB-auto-detected payments (the poller) and manual overrides. Where `invoice.status` and the project payment state live in the DB. What event/job chain fires after a manual payment confirmation — and what is currently broken (likely a missing state write or an incorrect redirect).
approach: Reproduce in staging: create an invoice, skip QB payment, click 'mark as paid' manually, observe the resulting invoice status and redirect destination.
Trace the manual mark-paid route (InvoiceController or ProjectPaymentController) to find where the state transition is incomplete or the redirect is wrong.
Fix the status write so the invoice lands in the correct paid state without a QB webhook firing.
Add a regression test: manual mark-paid → `invoice.status = paid` → project reflects the payment correctly.
resources: Invoice and ProjectPayment models (status state machine, QB poller path)
GS-ERP staging environment for live reproduction

tasks.title: Clickup Backfill
tasks.notes: Import all ClickUp projects that paid the first deposit and are in drawing stage. Exclude projects with approved design.

prep.what: One-time data migration: pull all qualifying ClickUp projects (first deposit paid + in drawing stage, not yet approved design) into GS-ERP as active project records.
prep.understand: The GS-ERP project/order data model (required fields: client, product type, stage, measurements, order ref). How ClickUp represents project stages and payment status. What 'approved design' looks like in ClickUp so you can exclude those correctly.
approach: Export or API-query ClickUp — get all projects, then filter to: first deposit paid AND status = drawing stage, excluding any with approved design status.
Map ClickUp fields to GS-ERP project model: client name → Lead/Customer, ClickUp status → GS stage, description → notes, financial fields → order references.
Build or run the import script — create GS-ERP project/order records in bulk, with a duplicate-check gate so re-runs are safe.
Run in staging first to verify field mapping and record integrity, then run on prod with a rollback plan ready.
resources: ClickUp API or admin export (your ClickUp workspace access)
GS-ERP project/order creation routes (ProjectController or any import tooling under `app/Jobs/` or `app/Services/`)

tasks.title: Add PerLinearFt RateType (prereq for trim pricing)
tasks.notes: RateType has no per-linear-foot case. Add PerLinearFt='per_linear_ft', wire unitFromRateType to return 'lf', seed a per-LF trim LaborRate. Must land before t48.

prep.what: Add a `per_linear_ft` case to the RateType enum and wire it through LineItemFactory so LaborRates can be priced per linear foot — the prerequisite for pricing trim and wall-linear takeoff lines.
prep.understand: The `RateType` enum structure and how `LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType()` maps rate types to line-item unit strings (sqft → sf, ea, lf). How `LaborRateSeeder` seeds rates that the estimate seeder consumes downstream.
approach: Add `PerLinearFt = 'per_linear_ft'` to `app/Enums/RateType.php` with a readable label.
In `LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType()`, return `'lf'` for the `PerLinearFt` case.
Add a per-LF trim `LaborRate` row to `LaborRateSeeder.php`.
Run PHPUnit — confirm the suite stays green with no seeder or factory regressions.

tasks.title: Route takeoff measurements to trades at the seam
tasks.notes: Every measurement collapses into one anonymous $0 custom line today. Need to switch on kind (area/line/count) and tag each line with the correct trade via the core-vs-subbed helper.

prep.what: Fix `TakeoffEstimateSeeder` to preserve the engine's measurement kind and route each line to the right trade: area(SF)→flooring, derived wall SF→painting, line(LF)→trim/wall-linear, count(EA)→doors/tile. Tag each line as self-perform or subcontracted.
prep.understand: The engine measurement schema: each measurement has a `kind` field (area / line / count) and a `unit` (SF / LF / EA). The `ProjectType` enum's `isCoreTrade()` and `group()` methods that classify painting+flooring as core (self-perform) and everything else as sub. What fields `TakeoffEstimateSeeder` currently discards when collapsing to a single line.
approach: Open `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` — trace the full loop from raw measurement to line-item creation to see exactly what gets collapsed and what fields are available.
Add a `switch($measurement->kind)` to route each measurement to the correct trade and set the right unit (sf / lf / ea).
Tag each line with a trade via `ProjectType::group()` or `isCoreTrade()` so the estimate reflects self-perform vs. subcontracted lines.
Test on staging: upload a real sheet, seed an estimate, verify lines arrive under the correct trade with correct units and real prices.
resources: Engine measurement schema (kind: area/line/count, unit: SF/LF/EA)

tasks.title: One-click 'Create estimate from this takeoff'
tasks.notes: Today seeding requires an existing estimate + manually typing takeoff_project_id. Add a button on the Review page that creates a draft estimate and seeds it in one action.

prep.what: Add a 'Create estimate from this takeoff' button to the Takeoff Review/Index page that atomically creates a new draft estimate and seeds it from the selected takeoff project — no manual estimate pre-creation or id-typing required.
prep.understand: The existing `estimates/{id}/seed-from-takeoff` route and `seedFromTakeoff()` in `EstimateController`. How a new blank estimate is created (POST /estimates with a lead_id). The Takeoff Vue and how it currently links through to estimate flows. What edge case arises if an estimate already exists from this takeoff.
approach: Add a new controller action (or extend the existing seam) that creates a fresh draft estimate for the current lead and immediately calls `seedFromTakeoff` with the takeoff project id — returning a redirect to estimate edit.
Wire a 'Create estimate from takeoff' button on `Takeoff/Index.vue` or the Review panel that POSTs to this action with the takeoff project id.
Handle the edge case: if an estimate already exists from this takeoff, offer to re-seed or navigate to the existing one (don't silently create a duplicate).
End-to-end test on staging: click the button → estimate created and seeded → land on estimate edit with the correct trade-routed lines.
resources: Staging CT Pros for live end-to-end verification
